newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Tax collection in Bogota called highly unreliable.
newsitem.headline: Tax collection in Bogota called highly unreliable.

text.p: The comptroller general's office issued a scathing report on tax collection in the Colombian capital Thursday, suggesting that the government has no real way of telling what its revenues are.
"The figures being handled are not reliable and this has led to immense doubts on real public revenues," the report said.
Bogota, which is home to most the biggest corporations and multinationals operating in Colombia, is responsible for 44 percent of the country's annual tax revenue.
The report said a whole catalogue of deficiencies had been found in an internal audit of tax collection services carried out between 1993 and 1995.
One of the leading problems is that banks receiving tax payments regularly hold onto them well beyond the deadline when they are supposed to have been deposited at the central bank.

It did not single out any bank by name, but said the gap between projected tax revenues and what actually enters government coffers was an ever widening one that was putting a serious drag on government spending.
